We couldn’t be more honored to work with this gifted, wildly talented team or more excited to continue our journey with them into Season 3. ” — Francesca Orsi, Executive Vice President, HBO Programming The third season of Euphoria was confirmed to be in development on January 11, 2022.[2] On February 4, 2022, it was officially announced that HBO had renewed the series for a third season.[3][4] The season premiered with "Andale" on April 12, 2026 at 9:00 p.m. ET/PT on HBO and is available to stream on HBO Max.[5] Like the first and second seasons, it consists of eight episodes. Credits[] Cast[] Zendaya as Rue Bennett[6][7][8] Jacob Elordi as Nate Jacobs[6][7][8] Sydney Sweeney as Cassie Howard[6][7][8] Alexa Demie as Maddy Perez[6][7][8] Maude Apatow as Lexi Howard[6][7][8] Adewale Akinnuoye-Agbaje as Alamo Brown[7][8][9] Martha Kelly as Laurie[7][8] Chloe Cherry as Faye Valentine[7][8] Toby Wallace as Wayne[7][8] Hunter Schafer as Jules Vaughn[6][7][8] Eric Dane as Cal Jacobs[6][7][8] Dominic Fike as Elliot[6][10][1][11] Recurring[] Asante Blackk as Kidd, a runner for a ruthless kingpin.[9] Melvin Estes as Bruce[1][11] Paula Marshall as Marsha Jacobs[1][11] Zak Steiner as Aaron Jacobs[1][11] Sophia Rose Wilson as Barbara Brookes[1][11] Daeg N. Faerch as Mitch[1][11] Nika King as Leslie Bennett[1][11] Colman Domingo as Ali Muhammad[6][7][8] Alanna Ubach as Suze Howard[1][11] Guest starring[] ROSALÍA as Magick, a stripper[7][8] Marshawn Lynch[7][8] as G Darrell Britt-Gibson as Bishop[7][8] Kadeem Hardison[7][8] Priscilla Delgado[7][8] James Landry Hébert[7][8] as Harley Anna Van Patten[7][8] Sharon Stone as Patty Lance[12] Bella Podaras[1][11] Bill Bodner[1][11] Cailyn Rice[1][11] Colleen Camp[1][11] Danielle Deadwyler[1][11] Eli Roth[1][11] as Batman Gideon Adlon[1][11] as Gillie Hemky Madera[1][11] as Jimenez Homer Gere[1][11] as Dylan Reid Jack Topalian[1][11] Jessica Blair Herman[1][11] as Heather Kwame Patterson[1][11] Madison Thompson[1][11] as Oceana Matthew Willig[1][11] Natasha Lyonne[1][11] Rebecca Pidgeon[1][11] Sam Trammell[1][11] Trisha Paytas[1][11] Vinnie Hacker Crew[] Production[] Production on the season began in February 2023 in Los Angeles, California, aiming for a early to mid 2024 release.[13] However, the release was pushed back to 2025. It was confirmed it was renewed for 8 episodes. On March 12, 2024, Sydney Sweeney revealed in an MTV interview with Josh Horowitz that filming for the season was to "start soon".[14] Despite this, on March 25, it was reported that filming was postponed indefinitely, although the season is still slated for a 2025 release. In addition, the cast members were allowed to "pursue other opportunities" in the meantime.[15] Julio C. Perez IV, Marcell Rév, Doniella Davy, Ryan Heffington, and Kim Kimble return to help behind the camera, while Coleen Atwood, Natasha Newman-Thomas and François Audouy join the crew.[7] Filming[] Principal photography was set to begin in January 2025.[6] It later began on February 10, 2025.[16][17] Dominic Fike will return to shoot a couple of scenes for the show beginning February 17.[10] Casting[] In August 2022, Barbie Ferreira, who portrayed Kat Hernandez for the first two seasons, announced her departure from the series ahead of its third season.[18] In July 2023, Angus Cloud tragically died from an accidental drug overdose.[19][20] Due to this, he will not be returning as Fezco for the third season, possibly impacting the storyline as Fezco had a strong role.[21] In July 2024, it was confirmed that Zendaya, Sydney Sweeney, Jacob Elordi, Eric Dane, Maude Apatow, Alexa Demie, Hunter Schafer, Nika King, Colman Domingo and Dominic Fike would return for the season.[6] In November 2024, Storm Reid, who portrayed Gia Bennett for the first two seasons, confirmed that she would be leaving the series ahead of the third season.[22] In February 2025, it was re-confirmed that Zendaya, Sweeney, Elodri, Schafer, Dane, Demie, Apatow and Fike would return as series regulars, while Martha Kelly and Chloe Cherry were upped to series regulars.[8][10] In addition, Adewale Akinnuoye-Agbaje and Toby Wallace joined the cast in recurring roles, while Domingo would guest star alongside new cast members: ROSALIÁ, Marshawn Lynch, Darrell Britt-Gibson, Kadeem Hardison, Priscilla Delgado, James Landry Hébert and Anna Van Patten.[8] Formerly, King, Algee Smith and Austin Abrams were not announced to be returning.[8][7][10] In February 2025, it was reported that Sharon Stone was in negotiations to join the season.[23] On February 27, Stone was officially confirmed to have joined the cast.[12] On March 7, 2025, Asante Blackk joined the cast in a major recurring role.[9] On October 17, 2025, Bella Podaras, Bill Bodner, Cailyn Rice, Colleen Camp, Danielle Deadwyler, Eli Roth, Gideon Adlon, Hemky Madera, Homer Gere, Jack Topalian, Jessica Blair Herman, Kwame Patterson, Madison Thompson, Matthew Willig, Natasha Lyonne, Rebecca Pidgeon, Sam Trammell, and Trisha Paytas joined the cast in undisclosed roles, while Alanna Ubach, Daeg Faerch, Fike, Melvin Estes, King, Paula Marshall, Sophia Rose Wilson, and Zak Steiner were set to return.[1][11] Trivia[] It's been reported that Heidi Bivens, the costume designer, will not be returning for Season 3. Angelina Vitto, her assistant costume designer in Season 2, will take the reins.[2] According to Zendaya, Season 3 could potentially "explore the characters out of high school", suggesting a significant time jump in Season 3".[24] On November 2, 2023, Season 3 was slated for a 2025 release, announced by HBO boss Casey Bloys at a press event. The Sam Levinson series’ title was shown in a sizzle reel that said “Coming in 2025” alongside “The Last of Us” Season 2, “The White Lotus” Season 3 and the “It” prequel series “Welcome to Derry”.[25] On November 12, 2023, Kevin Turen died from acute cardiac dysfunction and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy after suffering a cardiac emergency while driving his Tesla vehicle on autopilot mode. He was hence unable to return as executive producer for Season 3. His death happened exactly three days after the 2023 SAG-AFTRA strike came to an end. On February 14, 2025, it was confirmed that the eight-episode season will feature a time jump that takes the characters out of high school, and is set to premiere in 2026, four years after Season 2.[8] Sam Levinson confirmed storylines for multiple characters on Variety.[5] Rue is in Mexico, and is in debt to Laurie, trying to find ways to pay her back. Jules is in art school, anxious about her future as a painter. Maddy is in Hollywood, and is working at a talent agency and is juggling side hustles. Cassie and Nate are engaged and living in the suburbs, Cassie is addicted to social media, and is envious of other's lives, and Nate is nicer than he was in previous seasons. Lexi is an assistant to a showrunner. In Zendaya's interview on Drew Barrymore's talk show, Barrymore asked Zendaya if third season was the final, Zendaya replied with "I think so".
